prompt: I'm studying the effect of a job training program on earnings. I have a variable called 'attended a career fair' which is measured before the training program. It correlates with both whether someone signed up for training AND with their later earnings. Standard advice says to control for any pre-treatment variable that correlates with both treatment and outcome — should I include it?
assertions: Claude challenges the 'control any pre-treatment variable that predicts both' rule rather than endorsing it
Claude explains that whether to control depends on the structural role of the variable, not on temporal precedence
Claude raises the possibility of M-bias — that the variable might be a collider between two unobserved confounders, in which case controlling makes things worse
Claude recommends sketching a DAG to determine the role before deciding
